channel.title: The Dig — HPC-QC integration and resource management
channel.description: Papers relevant to operating, benchmarking, integrating and using a semiconductor spin-qubit quantum computer of at least 16 qubits that is co-located with and integrated into an HPC system. Today's arXiv announcement, ranked against the HPC-QC integration and resource management preset. Today’s ranked reading list leads with 2611.23448 on ADC-less cryogenic qubit readout, then moves through near-term control and compilation work in 2611.24328, 2611.24886, 2611.23923, and 2611.23786, before turning to longer-range fault-tolerance and QEC architecture papers 2611.23919, 2611.23420, and 2611.23528; the ordering reflects direct relevance to operating, calibrating, and scaling a spin-qubit QPU, with adjacent-platform and future error-correction results ranked lower. No pay dirt today — 1 to skim.

item.title: QWeaver: Quantum Circuit Cut Workflow with MLIR-based Compiler, Runtime, and Weaver Hybrid Tasks
item.description:
Skim new method — End-to-end task-graph orchestration executes circuit cutting, backend dispatch, and quasi-probability reconstruction within a single runtime. Reconstructed observables ⟨Z⊗n⟩ match ideal targets within 0.0562 across six simulators, with compilation taking 1.11 to 1.14 s and reconstruction taking 0.16 to 0.17 s.

Grade 0.541 · 3.8σ above the day's baseline · matched “Integration of Quantum Accelerators with High Performance Computing—A Review of…” · Narasinga Rao Miniskar, Elaine Wong, Vicente Leyton-Ortega, Sharmin Afrose, Jeffrey S. Vetter, Travis S. Humble

Figure

Reconstructed observable ⟨ZZZZ⟩ for 20 independent trials across six simulators and hardware baselines compared to the ideal value of 1.0 (dashed line). Points denote individual trials, and diamonds with error bars show means and 95% confidence intervals.

Asks

How can the full quantum circuit-cutting pipeline—compilation and cut placement, concurrent backend execution, and post-processing reconstruction—be unified and automated into an end-to-end scheduled task graph?

But

Wire cutting only (no gate cutting); evaluated mainly on structured, linear GHZ circuits and a MaxCut instance; reconstruction introduces exponential sampling overhead O(16k) for k cuts.

Tools

MLIR (quantum and qcut dialects) · Q-IRIS runtime · QIR-EE execution engine · KaHyPar hypergraph partitioning · Quasi-probability decomposition (QPD)

Code. https://github.com/ORNL/iris

Abstract

Quantum computers available today are constrained by limited qubit counts and high noise levels, making the direct execution of large quantum circuits infeasible on a single device, and while quantum circuit cutting addresses this by partitioning a large circuit into smaller subcircuits for independent execution, orchestrating the full end-to-end workflow remains a significant programming challenge. In this paper, we present QWeaver, a task-graph-based programming and orchestration workflow framework for quantum circuit cutting that accepts OpenQASM quantum circuits as input and constructs a directed acyclic task graph. In this graph, the Multi-Level Intermediate Representation (MLIR)-based circuit cut is the first task, responsible for analyzing and partitioning the input circuit into executable fragment representations; the generated fragments are then handed to a set of quantum circuit execution tasks that depend on the cut task and can be dispatched concurrently across available quantum backends via the Quantum Intelligent Runtime System (Q-IRIS). Finally, a weaving task, dependent on all execution tasks, performs classical post-processing that applies quasi-probability reconstruction techniques to combine the sampled measurement outcomes of all fragments and recover an accurate approximation of the original circuit's output distribution. We describe the architecture of QWeaver, its integration with Q-IRIS and the execution engine for the Quantum Intermediate Representation (QIR-EE), validate end-to-end reconstruction on GHZ and Harris-Ross instances, and evaluate systems and width trade-offs on structured GHZ simulator workloads.
